article.title: New York’s Blue Wave Results & Public Dissatisfaction with Democratic Leadership
article.author: The Thorn - NYC DSA Electoral Working Group
article.content: The Thorn is published weekly by the Electoral Working Group of the NYC Democratic Socialists of America . Join the Electoral Working Group ! Local News Since last week’s midterms, there has been widespread public outcry against the feckless Democratic leadership of Hakeem Jefferies and Chuck Schumer, with calls for them to make way for a more progressive/offensive leader. A Change.org petition has circulated, calling for Hakeem Jefferies to step down as prospective House Speaker for the incoming 120th Congress. It currently sits at over one million signatures. A likewise petition exists for Chuck Schumer to step down as prospective Senate Majority Leader, though it only boasts approx. one hundred thousand signatures. This outcry has also spread to Senate electeds and incumbents , including Bernie Sanders of Vermont, Annie Andrews of South Carolina, Abdul El-Sayed and Elissa Slotkin of Michigan, Adam Hamilton of Kansas, Troy Jackson of Maine, Peggy Flanagan of Minnesota, and Julianna Stratton of Illinois. Despite the backlash, however, Schumer remains intent with maintaining his role as majority leader. According to New York City Criminal Summons, a recently published data analysis reveals that the NYPD names East New York and the South Bronx as neighborhoods most liable for low-level criminal summons, such as loitering, panhandling, and loitering. Attorney General Letitia James won a lawsuit against Nassau County Executive & Republican gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman over his countywide ban on transgender people in sports. This lawsuit was filed in July 2024 after the ban was passed, and the verdict comes one day after Blakeman’s loss in the gubernatorial race. In the aftermath of Cornell University’s controversial revelation alleging a gang rape incident involving seven fraternity students, the school’s faculty senate votes “no-confidence” in its leadership. Governor Hochul signed S9051B, a law that calls on state regulation and protection against “companion bots” that are engaged with by minors. Election News New York Governor Kathy Hochul secured her reelection bid by a twenty-point margin over Republican gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman. This includes notable flips from Rockland, Nassau, and Suffolk Counties, who previously voted for Republican gubernatorial candidate Lee Zeldin in 2022. Mamdani-backed DSA candidates Claire Valdez and Daraliza Avila Chevalier won their House races in the 7th and 13th congressional districts, respectively. In New York’s 17th congressional district, Democratic candidate Cait Conley defeats Republican incumbent Mike Lawler. New York City voters approved all five ballot proposals to overhaul and streamline changes within the city government. The proposals were in regard to: Question 1: Streamlining the approval process for private usage of public spaces. Question 2: Reducing paperwork for businesses and nonprofits seeking city contracts. Question 3: Changes to street sweeping projects combined with reforms to city-owned and government properties. Question 4: Simplify construction processes by establishing a centralized system for applicants to navigate approvals across city agencies. Question 5: Addressing how much money New York City should set aside for future emergencies.
